newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Precious metals seen trending lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Precious metals seen trending lower.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold prices could move towards support at $340.00 per ounce on Friday after coming under pressure from a stronger dollar overnight, traders and chartists said.
Silver is likely to match the gyrations in gold, while platinum may come under downside pressure if support at $440.00 if significantly breached, they added.
GOLD - Seen trending lower against the backdrop of the recent stronger dollar but should find support at $340.00 per ounce during European trading on Friday.
"Gold could lower today, though I believe it will hold a tight range and not move below $340.00," a trader said.
"The main focus will be on the movements of the dollar."
The dollar was broadly steady overnight, while gold slipped slightly following a lower New York close.

The 10- and 30-day moving averages are currently hovering above the market and should offer resistance to upside moves. Breakout points at $345.50 and $346.50 are unlikely to be visited, traders said.
Referring to the Comex gold contract, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said he was looking for further tests of support towards $341.00 as the technical indicators continue to trend lower.
"To reverse this bearish sentiment resistance initially at $346.60 would have to be negated," Squires said.
At 0700 GMT spot gold was quoted at $341.00/341.50, down on London's Thursday close of $342.40/$342.90.
SILVER - Expected to consolidate but adopting a downside bias after registering a string of lower closes over the past week.
Traders and analysts said they were looking for support at $4.70 to hold to offset a retracement to the May 20 low of $4.60.
On the upside resistance was expected to emerge around $4.80 followed by the June 6 peak at $4.95.
At 0700 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.71/4.73, against $4.75/$4.77.

PLATINUM - Last week's short-covering bounce looks to be dissipating but the market is set to remain volatile in case of a glitch in Russia opening its export campaign to Japan next month. Due to administrative problems Russia has not exported any platinum or palladium to major consumer Japan since December.
"If the Russian do start to export prices are likely to ease further," one trader said.
However, the trader believed that even with exports from Russia the platinum market would still remain tight, which should help to limit downside moves.
A significant break below $440.00 support might see the market testing $430.00 near-term.
On the upside Thursday's high of $452.00 should offer initial resistance. A re-test of last Friday's $505 high was very unlikely, traders said.
At 0700 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $435.00/440.00, versus $440.00/$450.00.
